question.text: Meridian Special Situations Fund (Cat II AIF, trust) distributes the following FY 2025-26 pass-through amounts to its LP Ms. Anjali Verma (resident individual, top slab): INR 80 lakh interest income, INR 40 lakh dividend, INR 2 crore LTCG on unlisted shares (post-23-07-2024). What TOTAL amount will the fund withhold under Section 194LBB before distribution to her, and what is the CHARACTER of income in her return?

answer.text: TDS = INR 32 lakh (10% on 3.2 cr total); all treated as 'business income' in her return.

TDS = INR 32 lakh (10% flat on the entire INR 3.2 crore pass-through); in her return, each stream retains character - INR 80 lakh interest under IFOS, INR 40 lakh dividend under IFOS, INR 2 crore LTCG on unlisted shares taxed at 12.5% plus applicable surcharge and cess.

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 194LBB requires the Investment Fund to withhold 10% on non-business income distributed to a resident investor. Total non-business distribution = 80L + 40L + 200L = INR 3.2 crore, so TDS = 3.2 crore x 10% = INR 32 lakh. In Ms. Verma's return, character is preserved under pass-through: interest is taxed under IFOS at slab, dividend under IFOS at slab, and LTCG on unlisted shares at 12.5% plus applicable surcharge and cess. The Trap: Option A wrongly blends all streams into 'business income' and ignores character retention. Option C applies the wrong TDS rate. Option D wrongly treats the pass-through as exempt from TDS. Note: The workbook supports 10% Section 194LBB withholding for resident investors, pass-through character retention, interest and dividend as IFOS in unitholder hands, and unlisted-share LTCG at 12.5% plus applicable surcharge and cess.
